text:
priya rao: Heads up — running into a weird UX/SDK interaction in the sampleapp. Using the JS SDK with a client-side token-bucket throttle + aggressive pagination (concurrency=8 prefetch=2). After a 401 during refresh, a bunch of in-flight page fetches restart and we end up fetching the same cursor/page twice. Anyone seen duplication like this?

mike chen: Yep saw something similar last week. Quick guess: token refresh path is causing requests to requeue without preserving request-scoped cursor metadata, so two different requests request the same cursor id. Are you mutating the cursor object in place?

priya rao: Not intentionally. We're passing a cursor obj down the pipeline and the paginator mutates cursor.next when it hands off to the worker. When the retry happens it looks like the worker picks up the mutated cursor state and replays.

sam lloyd: This smells like an in-place mutation + retry race. Two mitigation paths: (1) make cursor immutable / clone before enqueue, or (2) tag each fetch with a request_id and dedupe results by request_id on client. We added option (2) in our Go sample.

alex kim: small add — this also shows an SDK parity issue. Go/Py SDKs both had a token-refresh mutex that was process-global in older versions. If refresh blocks, queued requests wait then retry with a refreshed token but their local cursor refs may have been updated already. JS SDK used a per-client lock historically, so behaviors diverged. We need to standardize: per-token lock + preserve per-request state on retry.

emma: For the sampleapp guidance I'd recommend defaulting to lower concurrency for paginated endpoints (concurrency=3) and enabling a lightweight backpressure queue. Example snippet we use in sampleapp: 

```js
// simple token-bucket based throttle + safe queue
const throttle = new TokenBucket({capacity: 10, refillPerSec: 5});
async function fetchPageSafe(request) {
  await throttle.acquire(1); // backpressure here
  const reqCopy = {...request, _rid: uuidv4()}; // clone + id for dedupe
  return sdkClient.fetchPage(reqCopy);
}
```

mike chen: Also add jitter on retry/backoff and avoid immediate re-queueing of all in-flight requests after refresh. E.g. exponential backoff with random between 100-500ms. If the SDK's refresh handler blindly replays all pending promises, you'll get thundering replays.

priya rao: Good call. I noticed our retry path just re-resolves the waiting promises in order; no jitter.

ci-bot: Deploy: sampleapp/ux-throttle-fixes pushed to staging by @priya :rocket:

sam lloyd: One more data point — server-side cursor tokens often encode sequence info. If you include a small client-side nonce in each request and the server echoes it back, it's trivial to dedupe on the client if you get duplicate pages. Might be worth adding optional nonce param to paginated endpoints.

alex kim: Filed an SDK parity TODO. We should: (a) ensure refresh lock semantics match across SDKs, (b) document recommended concurrency thresholds in sampleapp, (c) add a sample for cursor cloning vs. dedupe.

priya rao: Plan: I'll open a PR in sampleapp with (1) cloning in paginator, (2) request_id dedupe opt-in, (3) jittered retry. Will also open GH issue for Go/Py parity. CCing eng-ml and devex channels.

mike chen: Thanks — if you want I can run a quick load test against staging once the PR lands to validate no duplicate fetches.

priya rao: That would be awesome. Thanks everyone.
